prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Regional Dispatch Center (alias Juniper), 24/7 regional EMS dispatch: intake, triage support, ambulance dispatch under clinical/jurisdictional protocols. Jurisdictions own resources/policy. Response zones (reviewed on road/population/agreement changes) have primary/alternate routes to Emergency Department and Riverside Trauma Center. Intake creates incident record; Center preserves original caller report with later clarifications (confirmed vs estimate); escalates readiness gaps to operational lead. Actors: - Call Taker Mara (alias Larkspur): location first (address, municipality, building/floor/entrance, landmarks, callback); age, consciousness, breathing, complaint, onset, hazards; observed vs reported; access barriers; produces Caller Location Correction Slip; updates record with new info before dispatch finalized; stays on line if info may change priority. Clinical triage begins after Mara captures symptoms, location, hazards; initial urgency, reassessed as info arrives. - Triage Supervisor (alias Copperfield): assigns priority; reviews uncertain severity, conflicting reports, rapid deterioration; directs clarification without delaying urgent response; escalates ambiguous/severe cases to Medical Director when time permits; sends Pediatric Acuity Note. Priority by threat to life, time sensitivity, deterioration risk; immediate threat gets highest priority, prompt dispatch; others by harm from delay. - Regional Medical Director: clinical policy guidance; does not replace dispatch operational authority. - Dispatch personnel: apply protocols, seek clinical guidance beyond authority, weigh travel time, restrictions, weather, closures. - Shift Commander (alias Sundial): operational authority, conflicts, surge, escalation, repositioning; shall not override Medical Director policy or crew on-scene judgment. - Radio Coordinator (alias Mistral): monitors Regional Radio Network; shift-start checks. - Paramedic Crew: patient care; verify access before constrained routes; report barriers/readiness. - Hospital Liaison Desk (alias Kestrel): capacity, capabilities, contact pathways, destination compatibility; records constraints in incident notes; produces Bedside Arrival Receipt on confirmed arrival; must not delay intake. - Emergency Department. - Fleet Maintenance Cell (alias Bluejay): produces Battery Swap Voucher. - Data Quality Officer (alias Pebble): monitors records for missing/inconsistent/duplicated info; sends Duplicate Incident Audit Memo. Systems: Regional Radio Network; Ambulance Coordination Platform; Computer Aided Dispatch Console (validates locations); Ambulance Unit 417; North Gate Status Board (produces North Approach Queue Snapshot); South Gate Status Board. Boards checked at shift start/access

New part:
S089: Data Quality Officer flags data defects for review but does not independently change a clinical priority.
S090: Computer Aided Dispatch Console presents the current incident details and assigned priority to authorized dispatch staff.
S091: Ambulance Coordination Platform uses the recorded priority alongside unit availability and operational constraints when coordinating response resources.
S092: Radio Coordinator communicates dispatch instructions and priority changes over Regional Radio Network.
S093: Paramedic Crew reports material changes in patient condition so that the incident can be reassessed promptly.
S094: Ambulance Unit 417 follows the active dispatch instructions and requests clarification when the incident details do not support safe response.
S095: Emergency Department may provide operationally relevant capacity information, while clinical triage remains governed by approved regional protocols.
S096: Riverside Trauma Center is considered for destination coordination when the patient's needs and current clinical guidance support that option.
S097: Shift Commander is notified when competing high-priority incidents exceed available response capacity or require an operational exception.
S098: Data Quality Officer reviews whether priority changes and their supporting rationale are recorded consistently for later assessment.
S099: Regional Dispatch Center preserves the original caller report alongside subsequent clarifications so responders can distinguish confirmed details from estimates.
S100: Triage Supervisor reviews significant disagreements about urgency and records the basis for the final operational priority.
S101: Resource selection begins after the operational priority and essential response requirements have been confirmed.
S102: The Ambulance Coordination Platform presents units whose reported status and capabilities match the incident requirements.
S103: The Computer Aided Dispatch Console displays estimated travel times, unit availability, and relevant access constraints.
S104: The Triage Supervisor confirms that the selected response level remains consistent with the caller information.
S105: The selection decision weighs clinical need, travel time, vehicle capability, crew readiness, and regional coverage.
S106: The Fleet Maintenance Cell provides current information about vehicles that are unavailable or restricted.
S107: The Radio Coordinator checks that the proposed unit can be reached on the Regional Radio Network.
S108: A dispatcher may recommend a unit, but dispatch authorization must follow the current regional approval rules.
S109: The Shift Commander approves exceptions that would materially reduce local coverage or require a nonstandard response.
S110: The Regional Medical Director may advise on clinical resource requirements when the incident presents an unusual care need.
S111: The dispatcher records the authorized unit and any conditions attached to its assignment.
S112: Regional Dispatch Center produces the Unit Staging Change Card when a previously selected unit must be repositioned.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
